label: Scientific Thinking
author: Neuron core curriculum
blurb: The working practices of research: reading a paper properly, reviewing one, handling data honestly, and writing up what you found including the parts you did not want.
scope: Domain practices, not cognitive constructs. Nothing here claims to be a latent ability or to have transfer evidence — these are craft skills with clear success criteria, which is exactly why they belong in a pack rather than in the core.

nodes.label: Reading a Paper Properly
nodes.description: Working through a primary research paper in the order that actually tells you whether to believe it: methods and sample first, then results, then the abstract last, checking what the authors claim against what they measured.
nodes.limitations: Reading well does not substitute for domain knowledge. In an unfamiliar field you will miss the methodological problems that are obvious to everyone who works in it.

exercises.label: Read one paper's methods before its abstract and predict the effect size
Write the gap between what a paper measured and what its abstract claims

resources.title: How to Read a Paper — Trisha Greenhalgh
Why Most Published Research Findings Are False — Ioannidis (2005)

nodes.label: Writing a Review
nodes.description: Producing a review that would improve the paper: specific, prioritised, separating fatal problems from fixable ones, and stating what evidence would change your recommendation.
nodes.limitations: Reviewing trains critique, not production. Reviewers routinely miss errors they would make themselves, and a good review does not imply you could have written a better paper.

exercises.label: Write a structured review of a preprint: fatal, major, minor, in that order

resources.title: Estimating the Reproducibility of Psychological Science — OSC (2015)

nodes.label: Data Hygiene
nodes.description: Keeping analysis honest and reproducible: a raw dataset that is never edited, a script that regenerates every figure, and every exclusion recorded with its reason at the time it was made.
nodes.limitations: Reproducibility is not correctness. A perfectly reproducible pipeline can implement the wrong analysis flawlessly.

exercises.label: Regenerate every figure in one analysis from raw data with a single command
Write the exclusion log for one dataset, with the reason recorded before seeing the result

resources.title: The Turing Way: Guide for Reproducible Research

nodes.label: Writing Up a Null Result
nodes.description: Reporting what you found when it is not what you hoped: stating the result with its uncertainty, distinguishing 'no effect' from 'no evidence of an effect', and resisting the reframe that makes it publishable.
nodes.limitations: This is a writing and integrity skill. It does not make null results easier to publish, which remains the actual obstacle.

exercises.label: Write up a result that went against you, without softening the conclusion
progression: Send it to someone who wanted the other result and record their response

resources.title: Error and the Growth of Experimental Knowledge — Mayo (1996)
